summary: Feed s114_double is degraded for IDS: 28.9% of frames truncated to 256 bytes and 58.0% still ERSPAN-encapsulated. IDS requires full payload and inner headers, so both faults severely reduce detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker has payload slicing/truncation enabled at 256 bytes, likely to save bandwidth to the 1Gbps IDS port. 513 of 1773 frames (28.9%) are forwarded cut short instead of full 1518 byte frames.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true for signature matching, protocol decoding and file/exploit detection. Truncated payloads hide application content, so IDS will miss payload-based alerts and create incomplete flow reassembly.

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot inspect truncated packets; disable slicing on this feed to deliver full payload. Use filtering or load balancing instead if 1G port is oversubscribed.

findings.root_cause: Traffic sourced via ERSPAN SPAN session is forwarded through broker without decapsulation. 1029 of 1773 frames (58.0%) still carry ERSPAN encapsulation, so tool sees outer tunnel headers not inner original packets.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS parses outer ERSPAN/IP/GRE instead of inner Ethernet/IP 5-tuple. It cannot correlate flows, apply signatures, or detect lateral movement on 58% of traffic - effectively blind to majority of feed.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to strip ERSPAN headers and forward inner original packets so IDS sees true endpoints and payloads for detection.
